title: Ctrl-C recorded as task failure

answer.patch:
--- a/runner.py
+++ b/runner.py
@@ -18,6 +18,8 @@ def run_tasks(
         tid = task["id"]
         try:
             row = run_one(task)
+        except (KeyboardInterrupt, SystemExit):
+            raise
         except BaseException as e:  # noqa: BLE001
             row = {
                 "task": tid,
answer.reason: When a user interrupts a long suite with Ctrl-C, a KeyboardInterrupt exception is raised. Currently, runner.py catches BaseException which includes KeyboardInterrupt, causing a scored failure row to be written instead of allowing the process to terminate cleanly. By catching KeyboardInterrupt and SystemExit separately and re-raising them, the process will terminate cleanly without writing a failure row.

title: Chat timeout_s never reaches HTTP client

answer.patch:
--- a/chat/wrap.py
+++ b/chat/wrap.py
@@ -16,12 +16,12 @@
     max_tokens: int = 1024,
     retry: int = 1,
 ) -> dict[str, Any]:
-    del timeout_s
     last: dict[str, Any] | None = None
     for _ in range(max(1, retry)):
         last = api.post_chat(
             model,
             messages,
+            timeout_s=timeout_s,
             temperature=temperature,
             max_tokens=max_tokens,
         )
answer.reason: In chat/wrap.py, the timeout_s parameter is received but then deleted with 'del timeout_s' on line 19, and it is never passed to api.post_chat(). This causes the HTTP layer to always see None for the timeout. The fix removes the 'del timeout_s' line and adds timeout_s=timeout_s to the api.post_chat() call.

title: Timed-out child with stderr-only output loses diagnostics

answer.patch:
--- a/util/subprocess_timeout.py
+++ b/util/subprocess_timeout.py
@@ -56,7 +56,7 @@ def subprocess_with_hard_timeout(
         proc.wait(timeout=10)
         stdout = e.stdout if e.stdout else ""
         stderr = e.stderr if e.stderr else ""
-        if str(stdout).strip():
+        if str(stdout).strip() or str(stderr).strip():
             return subprocess.CompletedProcess(
                 args=cmd,
                 returncode=-9,
answer.reason: When a subprocess times out and only writes to stderr (no stdout), the code raises ProcTimeout instead of returning a CompletedProcess with the stderr information. The condition only checks stdout, so stderr-only output is lost. Changing the condition to also check stderr ensures that any output (stdout or stderr) results in a CompletedProcess being returned with diagnostics.

title: Warmup ignores short timeout

answer.patch:
--- a/warmup.py
+++ b/warmup.py
@@ -9,4 +9,4 @@ from miniharness import config
 
 
 def warmup(model: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
-    _ = config.FIRST_BYTE_S
-    return chat(model, "Reply with exactly: OK")
+    _ = config.FIRST_BYTE_S
+    return chat(model, "Reply with exactly: OK", timeout_s=config.DEFAULT_WARMUP_TIMEOUT_S)
--- a/chat/wrap.py
+++ b/chat/wrap.py
@@ -16,10 +16,10 @@ def chat_wrapped(
     max_tokens: int = 1024,
     retry: int = 1,
 ) -> dict[str, Any]:
-    del timeout_s
     last: dict[str, Any] | None = None
     for _ in range(max(1, retry)):
         last = api.post_chat(
             model,
             messages,
+            timeout_s=timeout_s,
             temperature=temperature,
             max_tokens=max_tokens,
         )
answer.reason: The warmup path was not failing fast against a wedged backend because: 1) warmup.py did not pass a timeout to the chat call, and 2) chat/wrap.py explicitly discarded the timeout_s parameter with 'del timeout_s' instead of passing it to the API layer. By passing config.DEFAULT_WARMUP_TIMEOUT_S (30s) to the chat call in warmup.py and removing the 'del timeout_s' while forwarding it to api.post_chat, the warmup path will now fail fast on the order of tens of seconds instead of inheriting the suite's first-byte budget.
